A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Safe In-Context Reinforcement Learning, with complete main text and Appendices A–E. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v3 reports original simulation experiments comparing SCARED with baselines in Section 5, together with the noise-distillation comparison and ablations in Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v4 retains the original simulation experiments and appendix analyses, with revised results in Figure 2.

M1.justification: The CTG-conditioned policy, single-multiplier exact-penalty objective, actor-critic implementation, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate SafeDarkRoom, SafeDarkMujoco with Point and Car, and SafeVelocity with HalfCheetah and Ant. The center-to-edge distribution shift and held-out velocity tasks are unchanged.

E2.justification: Figures 1–2 retain safe AD, MAML with penalty, and SafeMeta. The appendix comparisons involving AD-EPS and naive primal-dual optimization also retain the same comparators.

E3.justification: Sections 5.2–5.3 and Appendix C report identical task splits, CTG ranges, 100-target averaging, metrics, training budgets, and model settings. No protocol revision is documented for the changed Figure 2 results.

E4.justification: The existing test of sensitivity to safety budgets receives revised return and cost evidence for SafetyHalfCheetah and SafetyAnt in Figure 2. Its scope and tested question remain the same; the analyses in Appendices D–E are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same standard-error shading and averaging descriptions. Changed uncertainty bands in Figure 2 do not introduce a different statistical reporting practice, run count, or estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 2 roughly halves SCARED and SafeMeta total returns in SafetyHalfCheetah and SafetyAnt, from around 5,000 to 2,500 for SCARED and 4,000 to 2,000 for SafeMeta. SafeMeta's maximum-cost curves also change. These limited revisions preserve the main rankings and broad budget-response findings; the other reported results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Assumptions 1–2, Theorem 1, Proposition 1, and their proofs in Appendix B are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about introducing safe ICRL, SCARED's adaptation without parameter updates, budget responsiveness, and generalization benchmarks.

C2.justification: The interpretations of budget responsiveness and baseline behavior are unchanged despite the revised curves. The applicability conditions and limitations concerning cost signals, budget selection, unmodeled hazards, and convergence proofs are also retained.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1, Appendix C implementation and data-collection details, Tables 1–4, and the code-release information are unchanged. No additional reproducibility information explains the Figure 2 revisions.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, and positioning relative to ICRL, safe RL, and safe meta-RL are identical.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv version/date stamp changes from v3 dated 27 May 2026 to v4 dated 23 July 2026. The prose, headings, and document structure are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 redraws the affected curves and uncertainty bands and changes the return-axis scales and tick spacing for SafetyHalfCheetah and SafetyAnt. Its caption, legend, placement, and panel arrangement remain unchanged, as do all other figures and tables.

improvement.justification: The substantive revision replaces several Figure 2 curves while retaining the same stated protocols, explanations, and conclusions. v4 does not explain whether these revisions correct earlier errors or reflect changes in the underlying evaluation. The PDFs therefore do not establish whether the revised evidence improves accuracy or overall paper quality.
